newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures fall after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures fall after data.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures erased early gains to turn lower in choppy dealings this morning.

Selling picked up after the release of the June Chicago purchasing mangers' index, which rose to 61.5 from 56.8 in May. Traders had expected a rise to 57.5. May U.S. single-family home sales also rose 7.1 percent to 825,000 units, the largest increase since November of last year.
Bond prices dropped after the data, and S&P 500s followed, falling more than 7.00 points before paring losses before recvering and then falling further.
Septebmer S&P 500s dropped below support at 896.10, 894.50, and key support at 892.75 on the decline. Further significant support is at the 2-1/2 week low of 880.65.
Traders said activity may have been curtailed a bit ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which begins Tuesday, and the release of June U.S. employment data scheduled for Thursday.
Traders said no policy change on the part of the Fed is expected.
Markets will be closed Friday in observance of the U.S. July Fourth holiday.
Some traders had expected prices to firm as the day progresses as end of the month buying props up prices.
However, weakness in the bond market may overcome such sentiment and temper buying interest.

"Bonds are kind of dragging us down," said one S&P 500 trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "If bonds weren't trading where they are, we would be in the 900's," the trader said of the September S&P 500 contract.
There was no reaction to personal income and consumption data released early this morning, which came in close to forecasts.
Traders pegged the theoretical fair value premium of September S&Ps at about 8.15 points, with buy programs liked at a premium of 9.50 points and sell programs probable at 7.00 points or narrower.

At 0912 CDT, June S&P 500s were off 5.50 points at 891.40, Nasdaq 100s were 3.65 lower at 971.50, KCBT Value Line futures were down 3.25 points to 790.00, Nikkei 225 index futures eased 70.0 to 20,555.0 and Midcap 400s fell 0.65 points to 290.20.
